findings.title: All 5 Blog media items have focal point at the far-left edge (left: 0), so every rendered crop is anchored hard left
findings.rule: Correctness concern, not an UMBRACO-RULES violation: GetCropUrl respects the stored focal point. No other violations were found: all 7 new document types sit in Blocks or Pages, the 5 blocks are isElement=true with no compositions, the 2 new data types are under Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid, aliases are camelCase, media is in the 'Blog' folder, the content root holds only WWW, the front page has domain '/', and uSync files exist for every new content type, data type, template, media item and content node. All 3 URLs returned 200 with no 'Could not render component', and all 7 returned 200 image/jpeg.
findings.evidence: Every Media/*.config umbracoFile has "focalPoint": { "left": 0, "top": 0.5 }. The rendered img URLs all carry rxy=0,0.5, e.g. /media/fgypfgmf/city-lights-from-orbit.jpg?rxy=0,0.5&width=2000&height=900&... (hero on /). The 2000x900 hero crops and 800x450 card crops therefore show the left edge of each Unsplash photo instead of its center.
findings.fix: Reset each image's focal point to the center (left 0.5, top 0.5) or to the actual subject, via update-media or the backoffice, and let uSync re-export. For future create-media calls from a URL, pass focalPoint {left:0.5, top:0.5} explicitly and read it back afterwards.

label: verify:schema-and-content:All 5 Blog media items have focal point

result.reasoning:
The stored data is as described, but the claimed effect doesn't happen, and no rule in AGENTS.md or UMBRACO-RULES.md covers focal points.

What checks out:
- All 5 files under Media/*.config store focalPoint {left: 0, top: 0.5}.
- The rendered image URLs carry rxy=0,0.5.

Why the crops are not anchored hard left:
- The source images in wwwroot/media are 2000x1333 (ratio 1.5), 2000x1331 (1.5) and 2000x1122 (1.78).
- The only crops in use are:
  - GetCropUrl(2000, 900), ratio 2.22, for the hero
  - GetCropUrl(800, 450), ratio 1.78, for the post cards
  - GetCropUrl(width: 1600) with no height, for the image block, which only resizes and does not crop
- Every target ratio is as wide as or wider than its source. Cropping to fill therefore keeps the whole width and trims only the top and bottom. The vertical focal value is 0.5, so that trim is centred.
- The horizontal value (left = 0) has nothing to act on. The one exception is server-racks (1.7825) at 16:9 (1.7778), which is about 5px wider than the target, and that image appears only in a width-only resize anyway.

Result: no rendered image shows "the left edge instead of the center". The finding is a harmless oddity in the stored data (it probably comes from how create-media sets defaults), not a correctness defect or a rule violation. At most it would matter if someone later added a portrait-style or narrower crop.

findings.title: Image block alt text repeats the caption, so screen readers hear it twice
findings.evidence: Adapter line 8: `AltText = Model.Content.Caption ?? Model.Content.Image?.Name ?? ""`. The component then outputs the same string twice inside one
findings.fix: Use the caption only as the figcaption. Take alt from the media item: `AltText = Model.Content.Image?.Name ?? ""`, since the media names are already descriptive ("Friendly robot", "Server racks and cabling"). Better still, add an optional `altText` property to imageBlock. When the image is described only by its caption, use alt="".

findings.title: The AssignedContentItem null guard does nothing because the getter throws instead of returning null
findings.evidence: Lines 10-12: `Posts = Umbraco.AssignedContentItem is { } currentPage ? BlogPostService.GetLatestPosts(currentPage, Model.Content.MaxItems) : []`. The Umbraco 18 XML docs for P:Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.UmbracoHelper.AssignedContentItem say: "accessing this property will throw an exception if there is not IPublishedContent assigned to the Helper" (<exception cref="System.InvalidOperationException">). So the `: []` branch can never run. With no assigned page (for example a block preview or a non-front-end render), the adapter throws instead of showing "No posts yet". Normal front-end requests are not affected: https://localhost:44317/ returns 200 and lists both posts.
findings.fix: Read the routed page in a way that really can be null, e.g. `UmbracoContext?.PublishedRequest?.PublishedContent is { } currentPage ? ... : []`. Alternatively, catch the InvalidOperationException. Either way, keep the plain-model mapping in the adapter as it is.

findings.title: The machine-readable date in <time datetime> depends on the current culture, while the visible date uses the invariant culture
findings.evidence: Line 24: `datetime="@post.PublishDate.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")"` has no culture, but the visible text uses `ToString("d MMMM yyyy", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`. blogPost.cshtml line 11 has the same pattern. Umbraco sets the thread culture from the domain. On a culture with a non-Gregorian calendar (e.g. th-TH gives year 2569), the datetime attribute would get an invalid ISO date. The site is multi-site ready by convention, so another language could be added. Today the only domain is `/` with en-US, and it renders `datetime="2026-09-29"` correctly, so this is latent.
findings.fix: Format the attribute with the invariant culture: `PublishDate.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`. Change it in both BlogPostList/Default.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml.

label: verify:code-conventions:Image block alt text repeats the caption

result.reasoning:
The facts in the claim are right, but it doesn't meet the bar for a real issue.

What I checked:
- **The adapter.** `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/imageBlock.cshtml` sets `AltText = Model.Content.Caption ?? Model.Content.Image?.Name ?? ""`.
- **The component view.** `Views/Shared/Components/Image/Default.cshtml` writes that value into `alt` and writes the same caption into `<figcaption>`.
- **The live page.** On `/i-built-this-blog-by-talking-to-umbraco/`, the `alt` attribute and the `<figcaption>` hold the same caption text.

Why it is still not real:
- **No rule requires it.** AGENTS.md (184 lines) and UMBRACO-RULES.md (14 lines) don't mention alt text, captions, accessibility, WCAG or screen readers. The reviewer's instructions say to mark an issue false when AGENTS.md or UMBRACO-RULES.md don't require it.
- **It isn't a correctness bug.** The alt text is present and not empty, so nothing breaks or crashes. Alt text that repeats a caption is a best-practice weakness, not a failure of a WCAG requirement.
- **The fix isn't clear-cut.** The suggested fix, a new `altText` property or taking alt from the media name, is a design preference. The media `Name` it proposes to use is a file-style label rather than real alt text.

It's a reasonable improvement to make, but it isn't a defect under the project's rules.

The technical observation is accurate, but I'm rejecting it as a required fix under the review criteria.

What checks out:
- Line 24 of Views/Shared/Components/BlogPostList/Default.cshtml and line 11 of Views/blogPost.cshtml both write `datetime="@....PublishDate.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")"` with no culture.
- The visible date text next to it passes `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`.
- `PublishDate` is a `DateTime` (Models/Blog/BlogPostCardModel.cs). Its `ToString` uses the current culture's calendar, so a culture like th-TH would indeed give a Buddhist-era year.

Why it isn't real:
1. No rule requires the fix. AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md say nothing about culture, globalization or date formatting. Searching them for "culture" finds only notes that some API calls take an optional culture argument. The claim's own "rule" is just "Razor correctness / date formatting".
2. The bug can't show up on the site as built. The claim itself says the only domain is `/` with en-US, and the attribute renders correctly as "2026-09-29".
3. The "multi-site ready" argument doesn't fit. In UMBRACO-RULES.md #9 and AGENTS.md line 36, it means adding sibling site Pages under WWW with their own hostnames. It doesn't mean adding languages, and it certainly doesn't mean non-Gregorian cultures.

Using `InvariantCulture` here would be good defensive practice. But it only guards against a hypothetical future setup with no rule behind it, and the instructions say to default to false in that case.

The claim holds up, but it has no practical effect today. What I checked:
(1) Lines 10-12 of X:/benchmarking/Umbraco.Bench/Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/blogPostListBlock.cshtml match the claim exactly: `Umbraco.AssignedContentItem is { } currentPage ? ... : []`.
(2) The Umbraco 18.2.0 XML docs in the nuget cache (umbraco.cms.web.common/18.2.0) say accessing the property "will throw an exception if there is not IPublishedContent assigned to the Helper", with `<exception cref="System.InvalidOperationException">`.
(3) Umbraco.Web.Common.dll 18.2.0 contains the throw message "Cannot return the IPublishedContent because the UmbracoHelper was not constructed with an IPublishedContent." That confirms the getter throws when no page is assigned instead of returning null. The nullable `IPublishedContent?` signature is misleading.
So the `: []` fallback can never run. Whenever there is no assigned page, the adapter throws instead of showing the empty state. This is a correctness defect in the guard, not a matter of style.
Caveats: this breaks no AGENTS.md or UMBRACO-RULES.md rule, and the project has no preview endpoint or Razor block-preview package that would reach that path, so front-end rendering is unaffected. AGENTS.md line 88 does mention rendering components from "a preview endpoint", which makes the non-front-end case plausible later.
Severity is low, as claimed. The suggested fix is reasonable: use UmbracoContext.PublishedRequest?.PublishedContent, or inject IUmbracoContextAccessor or IPublishedRequest.
